title: Swin-Transformer discovery of planetary nebulae with spectroscopic confirmation in VPHAS+
summary: A Swin-Transformer search of VPHAS+ Hα images identified faint, resolved planetary-nebula candidates in crowded Galactic fields that prior point-source searches missed. Follow-up spectroscopy and HASH classification of 31 targets found 16 true, two likely and four possible planetary nebulae, alongside contaminants and a supernova-remnant fragment. This is one validated search-sample result, not 22 equally secure confirmations.
ai_technology: Swin-Transformer deep-learning classifier trained on known planetary nebulae
organization: The University of Hong Kong; Taiyuan University of Technology; Peng Cheng Laboratory

evidence.tested: A Swin-Transformer search of VPHAS+ Hα images identified faint, resolved planetary-nebula candidates in crowded Galactic fields that prior point-source searches missed.
evidence.unknown: The 31 follow-up targets were selected from more than 800 high-quality candidates, so the sample is not a completeness or population estimate. Spectroscopic classifications comprise 16 true, two likely and four possible PNe; these confidence levels are not merged into a claim that all 22 are confirmed. Two non-emitter late-type contaminants and other emission-line contaminants were found. The result counts the paper-level AI-assisted search and validation campaign once.
evidence.ai_role: Scanned survey images and ranked candidate planetary nebulae; follow-up spectroscopy and standard HASH classification established which selected targets were nebulae and which were contaminants.
